title: Super Micro Computer Just Gave Its Investors Fantastic News
detail:
Super Micro Computer Just Gave Its Investors Fantastic News
David Jagielski, CPA, The Motley Fool
Mon, October 26, 2026 at 2:01 PM EDT 4 min read
SMCI
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ:SMCI) has earnings coming up and is scheduled to release its first-quarter numbers for fiscal 2027 on Nov. 3. And last week, the company gave its investors some great news: its results are going to be better than expected, with both revenue and gross margins coming in considerably higher than what they previously forecasted.

The company, which has been an integral player in the data center build-out, selling crucial artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, including servers and storage solutions, has benefited from significant demand for its products in recent years. This year, it's up around 12%, and a strong quarter could potentially light a fire under this lowly valued tech stock.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Revenue to be nearly four times what it was a year ago

Super Micro's upcoming quarterly results will be for the period ending Sept. 30. The company projects revenue in the range of $18.5 billion to $19.5 billion, a significant increase from its earlier guidance of $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion. Not only is that a big upgrade to the top line, but the tech company also expects its gross margins to be in the range of 12% to 12.5% -- higher than its previous projection of 10.4% to 10.8%.

These are extremely promising developments for investors for a couple of reasons. The first is the sheer growth. At $19 billion, the mid-point of its revenue forecast would mean that its top line will be nearly quadruple the $5 billion it generated a year ago. Margins have also been a key concern for investors, and if they are improving yet again, it's another encouraging sign that the business is making progress in the right direction.

Is Super Micro stock a steal of a deal?

Although Super Micro is experiencing significant growth, the stock itself isn't that expensive. Based on analyst projections, it's trading at a forward price-to-earnings multiple of just eight. The company has had accounting issues and governance concerns hanging over it in recent years, which may partially explain why the stock isn't trading at a higher valuation. Plus, there are concerns that a tech bubble has formed, and if demand for servers and other AI infrastructure slows, there could be significant headwinds for the stock.

Vertiv VRT is set to report its third-quarter 2026 results on Oct. 28.

For the third quarter of 2026, Vertiv expects net sales in the range of $3.65 billion to $3.85 billion. Organic net sales are expected to increase in the 34% to 36% range. The company expects adjusted earnings between $1.77 and $1.83 per share (43% to 48% year-over-year growth).

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for third-quarter 2026 revenues is pegged at $3.76 billion, indicating year-over-year growth of 40.63%. The consensus mark for earnings is pegged at $1.82 per share, which has decreased by a penny over the past 30 days. This indicates 46.77% year-over-year growth.

Vertiv's earnings beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate in all the trailing four quarters, delivering an earnings surprise of 12.61%, on average.

Let's see how things have shaped up prior to this announcement.

Factors to Note for VRT's Q3 Results

Vertiv's third-quarter 2026 performance is expected to have benefited from robust demand for power and thermal management solutions, driven by accelerating investments in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure and hyperscale data centers. Strong demand from hyperscalers, colocation providers, neocloud operators and enterprises is expected to have boosted demand for the company's power management, thermal management and integrated infrastructure solutions.

Vertiv is benefiting from significant margin gains. In the second quarter of 2026, the company reported an adjusted operating margin of 22.6%, up 410 basis points year over year and well above its previous guidance. This margin expansion was driven by disciplined operational execution, productivity improvements and favorable price-cost dynamics, partially offset by tariff impacts. The company expects margin momentum to continue in the second half of 2026. For the third quarter of 2026, adjusted operating profit is projected to be between $898 million and $938 million, with an adjusted operating margin of 24% to 25%, supported by organic growth, operating leverage and productivity.

Regional strength is expected to have been another key growth driver. Continued momentum in the Americas and Asia-Pacific, supported by strong data center investments, is likely to have boosted revenues. Improving demand conditions and strengthening order momentum in Europe, the Middle East and Africa (EMEA) are expected to have supported a return to organic revenue growth. Vertiv projected third-quarter 2026 organic sales growth in the high-30% range for both the Americas and APAC, while EMEA growth was anticipated in the mid-teens.

Vertiv's expanding portfolio of advanced power and liquid cooling solutions is also expected to have supported third-quarter performance. Increasing adoption of high-density AI computing infrastructure is driving demand for the company's integrated powertrain, thermal management and infrastructure solutions. Its growing capabilities in direct-to-chip liquid cooling and heat rejection, strengthened by the acquisitions of Strategic Thermal Labs and ThermoKey, respectively, are likely to have enhanced its competitive position and supported revenue growth.

However, VRT's third-quarter 2026 performance is expected to have been hurt by supply-chain congestion and execution complexities associated with large-scale infrastructure projects. Higher tariffs and increased investments in manufacturing capacity and R&D are likely to have weighed on profitability.

Super Micro Computer (SMCI) has recently been on Zacks.com's list of the most searched stocks. Therefore, you might want to consider some of the key factors that could influence the stock's performance in the near future.

Over the past month, shares of this server technology company have returned -23.9%, compared to the Zacks S&P 500 composite's -1.2% change. During this period, the Zacks Computer- Storage Devices industry, which Super Micro falls in, has lost 28.7%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?

Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision.

Earnings Estimate Revisions

Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings.

We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

Super Micro is expected to post earnings of $1.24 per share for the current quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +254.3%. Over the last 30 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed +6.4%.

The consensus earnings estimate of $4.74 for the current fiscal year indicates a year-over-year change of +30.6%. This estimate has changed +5.8% over the last 30 days.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $5.52 indicates a change of +16.5% from what Super Micro is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed +7.5%.

Having a strong externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool, the Zacks Rank, offers a more conclusive picture of a stock's price direction in the near term, since it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. Due to the size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, Super Micro is rated Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

Key Takeaways

Dell stock is down about 18.5% in the past month after Barclays downgraded it on Oct. 14, saying it sees no meaningful AI inflection in enterprise spending.

Barclays thinks higher memory prices are behind most of Dell's 58% revenue growth, which leaves sales exposed if those prices level off.

Dell's $95 billion AI backlog still stands, and Super Micro, down 21% over the same month, just reported preliminary quarterly revenue well above its own forecast.

Dell's fiscal third-quarter report on Nov. 24 will show how much of that backlog is turning into free cash flow.

Dell Technologies (DELL:NYSE) is down about 18.5% in the past month, trading near $459 on Monday. Most of that drop came on Oct. 14, when Barclays downgraded the stock.

Barclays wants to see AI in enterprise budgets

Analyst Tim Long cut Dell to Equal Weight from Overweight and trimmed his target to $574 from $603. He hasn't seen a "meaningful AI inflection" in enterprise spending. And he credits most of Dell's revenue growth to higher memory prices.

Barclays found that businesses spend only about 5% of their IT budgets on AI, with roughly a quarter of that on hardware. If memory prices flatten out, Dell's sales could too.

On Dell's fiscal second-quarter call, Vice Chairman and COO Jeff Clarke conceded, "There's a notion of inflation inside our growth."

The orders are still there

Price increases don't explain everything, though. In that quarter, revenue jumped 58% to a record $47.0 billion. Dell also booked $60.9 billion of AI server orders, and its AI backlog reached $95 billion.

Wall Street sees about $193 billion of revenue this fiscal year (ending January 2027), then $229 billion next year…

Super Micro Computer (SMCI:NASDAQ) backed up the demand side on Oct. 20. Its preliminary fiscal first-quarter revenue of $18.5 billion to $19.5 billion beat its own $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion forecast. Yet the stock is still down 21% in the past month.

Cheaper, but the cash has to show up

Dell now trades at 16x forward earnings, down from 26x in August. That's still above its five-year average of 12x.

AI server maker Super Micro Computer (SMCI) has had quite a ride in the market in recent years. Once celebrated as a key player in the AI infrastructure market and one of the primary beneficiaries of the same, faulty accounting and audit issues, along with accusations of chip smuggling to China, have derailed its progress.

However, the clouds may have started clearing after the company's preliminary results for Q1 FY2027 were cheered by investors in Wednesday's trading session. This has also led to leading Wall Street firm Wedbush deeming it a "clear positive." Elaborating on it further in a note to clients, analyst Matt Bryson of the firm said, "SMCI announced preliminary FQ1'27 results highlighted by revenue that looks to exceed prior guidance by ~$4B, with GMs also coming in above the guided range."

About Super Micro Computer

Founded in 1993, Super Micro Computer is an important supplier in the AI infrastructure supply chain. Rather than designing the GPUs that train and run AI models, it builds the surrounding systems, including servers that house GPUs, connecting them to memory and networking equipment, managing power and cooling, and integrating them into data centers. Today, Super Micro's operations span the United States, Taiwan, the Netherlands, and Malaysia, while claiming that a significant portion of its systems are designed, developed, and manufactured in-house, distinguishing its model from competitors that outsource more of their system assembly.

Valued at a market cap of $23.4 billion, SMCI stock is up 14% on a year-to-date (YTD) basis, only slightly outperforming the S&P 500 ($SPX). However, is this a false dawn? Let's find out.

The full Q1 results are slated to be released on Nov. 3, with the company having posted preliminary results several times before. Having said that, Super Micro expects revenues for Q1 to range between $18.5 billion and $19.5 billion, higher than the previous guidance of $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion. Encouragingly, the company expects higher gross margins too, expecting them to be between 12% and 12.5%, compared to 10.4% to 10.8%, earlier.
